clue.text: Huge solace in collapsing where one can put one's feet up

definitions.text: where one can put one's feet up

indicators.note: something collapsing falls apart, so the letters of the three words before it are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A great comfort when someone flops down into a seat at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsing' shuffles HUGE SOLACE IN, all twelve letters, into the French name for a long reclining couch.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise longue is a sofa with one extended end that supports the sitter's legs.

clue.text: Remove line specifying exeunt

definitions.meaning: to release the mooring rope of a boat
exeunt is the stage direction for actors leaving, so it tells the cast to go off

explanation.surface: A stage instruction about taking out a line of the script.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction 'they go out'; read the answer as the players being sent off stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means untie a boat's rope, and cryptically the players departing the stage.

clue.text: A pay increase is to occur

parts.note: a rise is a pay increase in British usage

explanation.surface: A pay rise is about to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to come about or happen.

clue.text: Long sentence not cut in possibly flowery work

parts.note: still means unmoving, unbroken, so not cut or interrupted
life is a life sentence, the longest prison term

explanation.surface: A prisoner's long term, uncut, spent producing ornate work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowery' looks like ornate prose, but the work is a painting of flowers, perhaps; 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a painting of objects such as fruit or a vase of blooms.

clue.text: Archbishop's double pops up

indicators.note: in a down entry, popping up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: dual means double

explanation.surface: A churchman's lookalike appears suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pops up' turns DUAL upwards. William Laud was Charles I's Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury, executed in 1645.

clue.text: One desiring to undergo Japanese drama? Not any more

indicators.note: in a down entry, going under places the desiring one beneath the drama

parts.note: No, or Noh, is classical Japanese masked drama
a longer is one who longs for something

explanation.surface: An eager actor who once wanted to try Japanese theatre, but has given up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to undergo' is read as 'go under', which only works in a down entry, where one piece can sit beneath another.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means formerly but not now, at an end.

clue.text: Too much not expected

definitions.meaning: read as ..., not due or awaited

explanation.surface: Something excessive and a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive, and split it reads as not yet owing or anticipated.

clue.text: This can produce neat movement with bouncing stride

definitions.text: This can produce neat movement with bouncing stride

indicators.note: movement of the letters of the word before it means they are shifted round

parts.note: a lope is a long bounding stride

explanation.surface: An animal that moves tidily with springy steps.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: 'This' is the animal itself, which bounds along with a springy stride.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a swift, graceful hoofed animal that bounds across the savannah.

clue.text: Stream over on signal

parts.note: a beck is a brook or stream in northern England
on means over, as in a lid on a box

explanation.surface: A creek crossed in response to a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: BECK is a northern English dialect word for a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to gesture to someone to approach.

clue.text: Some lords are not concerned with any matter

definitions.meaning: the Lords ... are the bishops who sit in the House of Lords, as against the Lords Temporal
relating to the soul rather than to material, physical things

explanation.surface: A remark that certain peers take no interest in anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The UK House of Lords includes senior Church of England bishops, called the Lords Spiritual; the first definition names that group.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of the spirit, unworldly and immaterial, and also names the bishops' bench in the Lords.

clue.text: Poet died at the stake

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
an ante is the stake put into the pot before a poker hand

explanation.surface: A writer meets a martyr's end, burned at the stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the stake' suggests burning, but it is a poker stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri is the Florentine author of the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Dramatist making a person sick

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one never knows'
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A playwright whose work turns someone's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was the American playwright of Long Day's Journey into Night.

clue.text: Beef joint to begin with is automatic

indicators.note: says the joint comes first in the answer, before the beef

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
jerk is beef or other meat cured by drying in strips

explanation.surface: A cut of beef described as reflexive, as though a butcher's roast moved by itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef joint' looks like one item of meat; split it into the beef and the joint, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A knee-jerk reaction is an unthinking reflex, made without deliberation.

clue.text: Strong, firm, and cold

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong
rigid means firm, unbending

explanation.surface: A list of three qualities, perhaps describing a stern character.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means very chilly, icy in temperature or manner.

clue.text: Just starting, Polar explorer's lost footing after short distance

indicators.note: says the explorer's letters come after the short distance

parts.note: an inch is a short distance

indicators.note: in a down entry the footing is the bottom letter, which is lost from the name

parts.note: Captain Lawrence Oates died on Scott's Antarctic expedition

explanation.surface: An Antarctic explorer slips just after setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost footing' drops the bottom letter, S, of OATES. Oates walked out to his death on Scott's 1912 South Pole expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means just begun, rudimentary and not yet fully formed.

clue.text: Become emotional, depressed by catastrophe

parts.note: to melt is to soften with feeling
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone weeps, gloomy over a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become emotional' looks like the definition, but the definition is the noun at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A meltdown is a disastrous collapse, originally of a nuclear reactor core.

clue.text: Marked down and reprimanded

explanation.surface: A pupil marked down and scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means checked off a list, and in British slang scolded.

clue.text: Divides up accommodation

definitions.meaning: lodgings, as soldiers' or servants' living space

explanation.surface: Someone splitting up rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means splits into four, and also means lodgings or billets.

clue.text: Put away, having broken down

definitions.meaning: a machine that has ... has stopped working

explanation.surface: Something stored away because it no longer works.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means tidied into storage, and colloquially failed or conked out.

clue.text: Quick to support father in church office

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece goes underneath the father

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
pacy means fast

explanation.surface: A fast-moving priest backs up his superior in a church role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' places PACY below PA in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the office of the Pope.

clue.text: Be conspicuous as second best

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: Advice on standing out when you have only come runner-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud colours are said to shout or yell, drawing every eye.

clue.text: Absurd lies accept by crazy fool

indicators.note: being accepted by the crazy word means sitting inside it

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: absurd means nonsensical, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Ridiculous falsehoods swallowed by a lunatic idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool' is a verb here, to deceive, not a noun for the crazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool someone is to deceive or lead them astray.

clue.text: Succeed old duke banished from Milan

parts.note: to prosper is to thrive or succeed

explanation.surface: A deposed nobleman makes good in exile.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's The Tempest the rightful Duke of Milan is ousted by his brother and cast away on an island.

clue.text: Strike horse with vigour

definitions.meaning: the Suffolk ... is an English breed of heavy draught horse
forcefulness, as in a speech with real impact

explanation.surface: Someone hits a horse hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the Suffolk Punch is a heavy English working horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means hit, a draught breed of horse, and forcefulness.

clue.text: Don't keep on soldiers neglecting duty

indicators.note: says the first piece is placed on, ahead of, the soldiers' letters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to miss an appointment is not to keep it

explanation.surface: An order to stop nagging troops who are shirking.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army; 'Don't keep' means fail to keep, as an appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss describes someone careless or negligent in their obligations.

clue.text: One judge is mad

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A judge has gone insane.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad here means angry, furious.

clue.text: Primate welcoming saint in part of church

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the primate's letters surround the saint

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey gives a saint a friendly reception in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, which fits the church picture, but here it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at a church's east end.

clue.text: Copper can do some discourteous driving

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A police officer is capable of rude manoeuvres on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman; here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut in is to pull sharply in front of another vehicle.

clue.text: Revision of page one is work done secretly

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Editing the front page of a paper is done behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revision of' rearranges PAGE ONE IS into the word for spying.
explanation.definitionFit: Espionage is spying, gathering intelligence covertly.

clue.text: Noble's seat in Northern town

definitions.meaning: a deep buttoned leather sofa named after an eighteenth-century earl
a town in Derbyshire, in the north of England, famous for its crooked spire

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's country house lies in a town up north.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a padded leather sofa, after the earl, and a Derbyshire market town.
